text:
This is a strange time. Now that Nvidia has their cards on the table, and AMD has set a bar for Navi...there's still a lot of unanswered questions.

Clearly Samsung 8nm isn't great. Can Nvidia snag some TSMC capacity? Is it even economically viable?

There will almost certainly be ti/super versions of the cards, and with better memory configurations.

That said, we now anticipate the 6800 to be on par with the 3070, 6800xt on par with a 3080, and 6900 to run with a 3090.

Still...where does Infinity cache run into problems? Is SAM worth a shit? What does ray tracing look like?

Then, of course, human malware, scalpers and miners are making things miserable for enthusiasts, so you can't even get your hands on any of this stuff.

I kept saying that 4k is viable now across a broad spectrum. Technically, that's true, but even if availability weren't an issue, it's still kind of a suboptimal time to buy without having more complete product stacks to look at independently.

Assuming AMD is right, and it seems they were with Zen 3, my thought is that a 5600x and 6800XT is a great value proposition that geta you at roughly 10900k + 3080 performance, and may even come very close to 3090 at a much better value both in terms of cost and power.
